papers.title: Holographically motivated Hubble-running dark energy: Phantom-divide crossing in VCDM and observational constraints
papers.authors: Antonio De Felice, Burin Gumjudpai, Shinji Tsujikawa, Jack Zidich
papers.abstract: Motivated by power-law dependences on the expansion scale in holographic dark-energy constructions, we study the Hubble-running equation of state $w_{\rm DE}=w_0(H/H_0)^q$ (HoloEoS), where $H$ is the Hubble expansion rate, $H_0$ and $w_0$ are the present values of $H$ and $w_{\rm DE}$, and $q$ is a constant dimensionless exponent controlling the running. We embed this history in VCDM, a type-II minimally modified gravity theory that propagates only the two tensor modes of general relativity. For regular expanding histories with standard matter, we reconstruct the potential $V(\phi)$ of its nondynamical auxiliary scalar field, providing a Lagrangian description of both the homogeneous background and cosmological perturbations. This framework allows HoloEoS to realize a smooth late-time crossing of the phantom divide $w_{\rm DE}=-1$. We confront this VCDM realization with SPT, Planck, and ACT CMB data, updated DESI DR2 distances, and optionally DESY5 supernovae with Dovekie recalibration, comparing it with $\Lambda$CDM and the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder parameterization embedded in the same gravitational framework (CPL-VCDM). For the full data combination, the posterior medians and central $68\%$ credible intervals are $w_0=-0.881^{+0.040}_{-0.038}$ and $q=0.453^{+0.143}_{-0.133}$, with a crossing redshift $z_\times=0.476^{+0.106}_{-0.081}$ conditional on $0<z_\times<6$. For this data combination, physical-likelihood optimization by Metropolis--Hastings (MH) simulated annealing gives Akaike information criterion differences of $\Delta\mathrm{AIC}\simeq-3.40$ for HoloEoS and $-4.10$ for CPL-VCDM relative to $\Lambda$CDM. Thus, a Hubble-scale-motivated dark-energy history realized within a specified gravitational theory achieves fitting performance comparable to CPL-VCDM while naturally allowing phantom-divide crossing.

papers.title: Full-shape analysis of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum and bispectrum: validation on simulations
papers.authors: Roger de Belsunce, James M. Sullivan, Mikhail M. Ivanov
papers.abstract: The Lyman-$\alpha$ (LyA) forest of neutral hydrogen provides a large-volume, high-resolution map of cosmological fluctuations from optical spectra at high redshift. To extract more information from the currently observing Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), we derive an effective field theory (EFT) model for joint full-shape analyses of the LyA forest data. It combines the one-loop power spectrum of the LyA forest (FF), and of its cross-correlation with dark-matter halos, used as proxies for high-redshift quasars (FQ), with the tree-level bispectrum of the LyA forest (FFF). Importantly, the bispectrum breaks the LyA-specific degeneracy between the mean flux and the amplitude of the power spectrum. We validate our theory framework on idealized large-volume LyA forest mocks painted onto the AbacusSummit N-body simulation suite at redshift z=2.5. Fitting scales up to $k_\mathrm{max}^{FF\,(FQ)}=0.6\,(0.3)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the power spectrum and $k_\mathrm{max}^{FFF}=0.1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ in the bispectrum, our full-shape analysis yields unbiased constraints on the cosmological parameters in simulations. For a fully sampled flux field in a simulated volume of $V=8\,h^{-3}\,{\rm Gpc}^3$, we measure the Hubble constant, $H_0$, to $0.6\%$, the matter density, $\Omega_{\rm m}$, to $1.6\%$ and the amplitude of matter clustering, $\sigma_8$, to $3.5\%$. Adding the bispectrum improves the constraints on $\sigma_8$ by $28\%$. We also demonstrate that the inclusion of the quasar one-loop power spectrum (QQ) and tree-level bispectrum (QQQ) further improves cosmological constraints by $\approx 35\%$ using $k_\mathrm{max}^{QQ,\,(QQQ)}=0.2,\,(0.08)\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$. Our theory framework enables full-shape analyses of high-redshift data from DESI and its successor DESI-II, enhancing knowledge of the growth of structure of the Universe during matter-domination.

papers.abstract: Euclid is expected to discover ~$10^5$ galaxy-galaxy strong gravitational lenses across ~14,000deg$^2$, requiring automated searches with high completeness and low false-positive rates. Despite advances in deep learning, the effects of training-set composition, image representation, and preprocessing on survey-scale detection remain poorly understood. We present an ablation study of the convolutional neural network used in the ECLIPSE strong-lens detection pipeline, evaluating different training configurations on a fixed test set. Using simulated and real Euclid data, we compare VIS-only and pseudo-RGB representations, FITS and JPEG formats, training-set composition, hard-negative selection, and multi-stage training. We also assess ensembling on ~67 million DR1 cutouts. Training-set composition and strategy strongly affect high-Recall performance. Omitting simulation based pre-training reduces high-Recall weighted average Precision by 83.7% for VIS-only and 74.5% for pseudo-RGB models. Negative-sample selection also substantially affects performance, while FITS yields modest gains over JPEG at high Recall (~2-5%). On DR1, the logit-mean ensemble improves average Precision by 28.0% and 39.9% over the individual VIS-only and pseudo-RGB models. Among ~70,000 candidates selected for visual inspection, it recovers 11,256 unique grade A (secure) and B (probable) lenses, compared with 9650 and 10,395 for the individual models. The branches show complementary ranking preferences, particularly for lenses benefiting from near-infrared information. Careful training-set design, realistic negatives, and multi-band ensembling improve survey-scale searches. Our final ensemble achieves ~80% Recall at the operational selection threshold, outperforming ablation models with higher global classification metrics and highlighting the need to optimise performance for realistic survey conditions.[Abridged]

papers.title: The Full-Shape Analysis of the Fading Dark Sector Model
papers.authors: Georges Obied, Cumrun Vafa, David H. Wu
papers.abstract: We analyze the Fading Dark Sector (FDS) model, which is motivated by string theory and in which the fading of the dark sector is driven by a scalar field. The model is specified by two $O(1)$ numbers $(c,c')$ that parametrize the logarithmic derivatives of the dark energy and dark matter densities with respect to the field in Planck units. In previous work, we showed that this model provides a good fit to the DESI BAO, CMB, and SN datasets. Here, we extend that analysis to include the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum, which adds information about the time evolution of cosmic structure and provides an independent consistency check of the FDS model. We find that, when the DESI DR1 full-shape data are combined with CMB+DESI DR2 BAO+DES-Dovekie, the FDS model outperforms the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization by $\Delta \chi^2_{\rm MAP}=-4$ at equal parameter count and is preferred over $\Lambda$CDM at $4.1\sigma$. The inferred values of $(c,c')$ with the full-shape data are unchanged from our previous analysis, so this improvement indicates that FDS makes a prediction for the growth of structure that captures the observed growth history better than the $w_0$-$w_a$ parameterization.

In this work, the authors adapt the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFTofLSS) framework in CLASS-PT to compute exact time-dependent 1-loop galaxy power spectra in redshift space for FDS without relying on standard Einstein--de Sitter kernels. They evaluate the model against the DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy power spectrum combined with CMB, DESI DR2 BAO, and DES-Dovekie SNe Ia data. The full-shape analysis breaks background distance degeneracies by testing structure growth predictions, demonstrating how modified dark sector dynamics fit recent cosmological tensions.

papers.title: Augmenting Galaxy Catalogues using Machine Learning in the FLAMINGO Simulations
papers.authors: Elliot Scott, Marika Asgari, Joop Schaye, Matthieu Schaller, Markus Michael Rau
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamic simulations are instrumental in the analysis of observations such as galaxy clustering used for the estimation of cosmological parameters. However, for these purposes, the simulations need both a large box size and high resolution, which is computationally prohibitive. In this work we use the connection between galaxies and their host dark matter halos to populate dark-matter-only simulations, using data from the FLAMINGO simulations suite. We employ the Extremely Randomized Trees algorithm to model the connection between the mass profile, history and environment of dark matter halos and the probability distribution of the stellar mass of the galaxy contained in the halo. We use halos matched between a dark-matter-only simulation and the corresponding hydrodynamical simulation to train a model for centrals. For satellites, we employ a Gaussian Processes emulator that simultaneously optimises the hyperparameters of a model and selects for the dark matter features that are predictive of the stellar mass while being insensitive to the differences between the hydrodynamic and dark-matter-only simulations, then train a model on only these features. We then apply these models to produce a new galaxy catalogue for the 2.8 Gpc FLAMINGO-10k dark-matter-only simulation as a product of this work. We demonstrate that this catalogue reproduces the statistics of the galaxy-halo connection predicted by the smaller volume hydrodynamical simulation on which the model was trained, including the stellar mass function, stellar mass-dark matter mass relation, 2-point correlation functions and correlations between stellar mass and dark matter concentration, half mass radius and dark matter mass within 3 Mpc.

papers.title: Multipoles in the IllustrisTNG simulation galaxies and implications for Strong Gravitational Lens modelling in Time-delay Cosmography
papers.authors: Abdullah Al Zaif, Suhail Dhawan, Vasily Belokurov, Erin E. Hayes
papers.abstract: Time-delay cosmography is a powerful independent probe of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), yet reaching the sub-2$\%$ precision required to resolve the Hubble tension demands a rigorous treatment of mass model systematics. We use realistic massive elliptical galaxies from the IllustrisTNG hydrodynamic simulation suite to characterise higher-order angular mass complexity in the form of multipoles ($m=1,3,4$) and quantify their impact on $H_0$ inference. We find that these multipole perturbations are common and emergent features of galaxy assembly; in 51$\%$ of our total samples ($54\%$ TNG100-1 galaxies and $85\%$ for TNG50-1 galaxies), the addition of multipole terms to a standard elliptical power-law model is preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion. Ignoring these structures in lens modelling introduces systematic biases in $H_0$: for perturbations of $\sim2\%$, the biases are of the order of 1--2$\%$ for $m=1$, 4--5$\%$ for $m=3$, and 3--6$\%$ for $m=4$ multipole. While the $m=4$ (boxy/discyness) mode induces a predictable directional bias, odd-order modes ($m=1,3$) introduce significant stochastic scatter. We demonstrate a degeneracy where unmodelled internal multipoles can be effectively absorbed by the external shear component. This combined with low signal-to-noise observations can create ``hidden biases'' where formally perfect fits to imaging data ($\chi_\nu^2 \approx 1$) could harbour significant cosmological errors. Our results provide an astrophysical basis for multipole priors and highlight the necessity of moving beyond rigid parametric models to achieve high-accuracy cosmography in the era of \textit{Euclid} and LSST.

papers.title: Note on quantum optimal measurements of CMB spectral distortions
papers.authors: Roshni Singh, Jacques Delabrouille, Daniel Carney
papers.abstract: As quantum sensing techniques continue to push the frontier of detection of ultra-weak signals, one may wonder if a sophisticated quantum strategy could be used to enable measurement of spectral distortions in the cosmic microwave background. Using quantum Fisher information techniques, we prove that the optimal strategy is simple frequency-binned intensity measurement. This proof strategy also enables us to provide numerical estimates for the information-theoretic minimum observation time required to observe the $\mu$- and $y$-distortions expected from $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. As case studies, we compare these results to the PIXIE and SPECTER mission concepts, and show that they are within a few orders of magnitude of this fundamental limit.

ai.summary: Spectral distortions of the cosmic microwave background (CMB)—deviations ($\mu$ and $y$) from an exact blackbody spectrum—contain valuable signatures of energy injection in the early Universe, but their detection requires extreme measurement precision. In this paper, the authors apply quantum Fisher information theory (a mathematical framework that determines the absolute maximum information extractable from a quantum state across all possible measurement protocols) to determine the fundamental limit of measuring CMB spectral distortions. They prove that simple frequency-binned photon counting (intensity measurement) is already the quantum-optimal strategy, both in the presence and absence of astrophysical foregrounds, because the thermal CMB photon density matrix has no phase coherence in the photon-number Fock basis. Using the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, they also derive theoretical lower limits on observation time for detecting $\Lambda$CDM-predicted distortions ($\mu \approx 2 \times 10^{-8}$), showing that proposed space mission concepts like PIXIE and SPECTER operate within a few orders of magnitude of this fundamental quantum benchmark.
conclusions: Frequency-binned photon counting is mathematically proven to be the quantum-optimal strategy for measuring CMB $\mu$- and $y$-spectral distortions, saturating the quantum Fisher information bound.

Exotic quantum sensing techniques (such as squeezed states or entanglement-based measurements) provide no fundamental sensitivity advantage over ideal photon counting because the CMB state is diagonal in the photon-number basis.
Ideal frequency-binned photon counting is inherently superior to Fourier Transform Spectrometers (FTS) because FTS spreads photon shot noise across all frequency channels.

Accounting for astrophysical foregrounds, the theoretical minimum observation time to detect $\Lambda$CDM-predicted $\mu$-distortions (at $\mu = 2 \times 10^{-8}$) with an optimized multi-horn satellite experiment is on the order of months.

papers.title: Predicting Individual Dark Matter Halo Concentrations from Their Assembly Histories
papers.authors: Dao-Zhou Wang, Weipeng Lin, Weishan Zhu, Tian-Cheng Luan
papers.abstract: We present an empirical model for predicting concentration parameters of individual dark matter halos in cold and warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies over z=0-5. Constructed using a large suite of cosmological N-body simulations, our model separately incorporates cosmic expansion (linear growth factor), mass scale (linear density fluctuations), halo mass assembly histories via the Extended Press-Schechter (EPS) scaled formation variable, plus a WDM damping term tied to the half-mode mass. It works for both virial and 200 $\rho_{crit}$ halo definitions. Across all tested cosmologies and redshifts, our global logarithmic fit gives concentration scatter ~0.09 dex for relaxed halos and ~0.09 to 0.10 dex for all halos. While relaxed halos maintain nearly constant scatter near 0.09 dex, the scatter of all halos at z>3 increases from 0.10 to 0.18 dex, revealing substantial violent-relaxation impacts on high-redshift halo structure. At fixed mass, concentration scatter is dominated by assembly history. We extract the scaled formation variable's probability distribution function (PDF) from merger trees and find departures from standard EPS theory. This PDF is narrower in WDM than LCDM due to suppressed small-scale perturbations and rapid, delayed monolithic collapse near the WDM truncation scale. Monte Carlo realizations with our formulae reproduce concentration distributions and match our prior peak-concentration model, whereas standard EPS underestimates concentrations from delayed-formation bias. Our framework offers a transparent, computationally lightweight tool to predict individual halo concentrations across diverse cosmological models.

papers.title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data

papers.abstract: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $\theta_i=\phi_i/f\in[0,\pi]$, conditioned on $\pi-\theta_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2\pi f)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $\Delta{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $\Lambda$CDM. papers.title: General $δN$ formalism in Single Field Inflation and Graph Theory
papers.authors: Amin Nassiri-Rad, Hassan Firouzjahi
papers.abstract: We study higher order correlation functions in single field inflation using the $\delta N$ formalism and methods from graph theory. By representing connected tree level contributions as graphs, we systematically classify their independent topologies, momentum shapes and amplitudes. We show that the amplitudes of arbitrary trees factorize into products of primary amplitudes, providing a general framework for relations among higher order correlators, including the Suyama-Yamaguchi equality. As the number of external legs increases, the number of distinct tree topologies grows exponentially, whereas the number of algebraically distinct amplitude products grows considerably more slowly. As an application, we consider ultra-slow-roll inflation followed by a transition to a slow-roll attractor. For transitions without a potential step, we derive an explicit all-order expression for the vertex amplitudes and establish their positivity and dependence on the sharpness of the transition. When a potential step is included, we prove that all nonlinear vertex amplitudes remain positive for upward steps, whereas downward steps allow cancellations at specific parameter values. These cancellations can eliminate entire families of tree contributions, including configurations in which the leading local bispectrum and trispectrum vanish simultaneously while higher order correlations remain nonzero.

They prove that any tree diagram's amplitude factorizes into a product of primary star-graph vertex amplitudes $a_d = N^{(d)}/(N')^d$, providing a structural explanation for generalized Suyama-Yamaguchi equalities. Applying this formalism to ultra-slow-roll (USR) inflation transitioning to a slow-roll attractor, they analyze how transition sharpness and potential steps impact vertex signs, identifying parameter choices where lower-order non-Gaussianities vanish while higher-order correlators persist.

papers.title: Distinguishing cosmologies with topological analysis of 21-cm hydrogen 2D brightness fields at Cosmic Dawn

papers.abstract: The 21-cm hydrogen line brightness field is a potentially valuable source of information about astrophysical parameters during the cosmological Dark Ages and the Epoch of Reionization. However, it can also be a source of observational data for cosmologists seeking to constrain cosmological parameters. We utilize topological data analysis to evaluate the possibility of such constraints. In particular, we use cubical complexes to perform persistent homology analysis of the 21-cm line brightness field. We generate 21-cm brightness fields of different cosmologies with the 21cmFAST package and then select snapshots at several redshifts corresponding to the Epoch of Reionization. Our goal is to find the redshift that is most suitable for highlighting the diversity between scenarios within a certain range of cosmological parameters. To compare persistent pictures built on simulations of the brightness field, we use Wasserstein distance, computed between any two persistent diagrams. We find that observations of the 21-cm field near $z=10$ have the potential to distinguish between cosmological models with different values of the normalized Hubble parameter $h_0$, the spectral index of scalar matter perturbations $n_s$, the matter density parameter $\Omega_m$, and the matter fluctuation amplitude $\sigma_8$, even in the presence of instrumental thermal noise. We perform the PERMANOVA statistical test on the matrices of Wasserstein distances to confirm this hypothesis for all considered cosmological parameters.

papers.title: Precise Deep-Learning Reconstruction of Galaxy Cluster Mass Maps and Substructures from Optical Observations
papers.authors: Atulit Srivastava, Weiguang Cui, Daniel de Andres, Guillaume Bonnet, Romeel Davé, Stefano Ettori, Massimo Meneghetti, Carlo Giocoli, Gustavo Yepes
papers.abstract: Accurately mapping the total mass distribution within galaxy clusters, including dark matter, is fundamental to understanding structure formation and constraining cosmological parameters. Furthermore, the subhalo mass functions derived from the reconstructed maps exhibit power-law behaviour broadly consistent with predictions from numerical simulations. Our results demonstrate that combining optical imaging with deep learning provides a scalable and physically meaningful approach to mapping galaxy cluster mass distributions. This framework opens a new avenue for exploiting upcoming wide-field imaging surveys to systematically investigate dark matter substructures across large cluster samples, complementing traditional gravitational lensing techniques. Moreover, the model is inherently flexible and can incorporate multi-wavelength observations, including X-ray and Sunyaev--Zel'dovich data, to further improve total mass predictions.

papers.title: Probing baryonic feedback using fast radio bursts and galaxy surveys

papers.abstract: The dispersion measure (DM) of fast radio bursts (FRB) provides a noisy measure of the free-electron column density to the burst. Comparing the DM auto-spectrum, DM-shear cross-spectrum and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect, we argue that the cross-correlation of FRB catalogs with galaxy surveys offers many advantages. Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT), often used in large-scale structure cosmology, is capable of modeling the clustering of electrons jointly with galaxies and matter to small scales. Using HEFT with the Padé model of baryonic feedback, we forecast that next-generation FRB surveys (combined with galaxy samples) will be able to constrain feedback at a level informative for Stage IV weak lensing surveys. In particular we should not be limited by modeling the manner in which galaxies trace the matter field. Rather constraints of the higher-order electron biases and the electron-galaxy cross-stochasticity provide the dominant limitation, and are an obvious target for improvement in order to reach percent-level constraints. The same measurements also provide a valuable means of constraining feedback in hydrodynamic simulations of galaxy formation in a way that is not tied to the modeling of particular galaxy samples.

papers.title: Parity conservation of the isotropic galaxy 4PCF in redshift space
papers.authors: Chanasorn Kongprachaya, Nicola Bartolo, Daniele Bertacca, Sabino Matarrese
papers.abstract: Recent observational investigation of cosmological Parity Violation (PV) through the galaxy Four-point Correlation Function (4PCF) has motivated a careful theoretical examination of potential systematic contributions. In this work, we demonstrate that parity-odd contributions to the isotropic 4PCF estimator induced by Redshift Space Distortion (RSD), up to the leading order $\mathcal{H}/k$ of general relativistic corrections, vanish upon averaging over all the Line-of-Sight (LOS). We analyse the perturbative relativistic galaxy number density, combining the biased tracer expansion and the dark matter gravitational dynamics within the framework of Standard Eulerian Perturbation Theory (EPT) to third order in the density perturbation. Building on prior studies of the parity-odd mode of the trispectrum (the Fourier-space counterpart of the 4PCF), we extend existing results in three directions: incorporating the wide-angle effect by adopting a local LOS definition for each galaxy in the 4PCF, accounting for tidal bias in the galaxy population, and generalising the assessment to an arbitrary cosmological background. Expanding the 4PCF in spherical harmonics, we show that angular momentum selection rules, encoded in the Wigner 3-j symbols, enforce that only parity-even contributions survive the integration over all LOS orientations, both in the plane-parallel approximation and in the full wide-angle case. This result is crucial for large-scale statistical analyses using isotropic estimators. It supports interpreting possible PV detections as a signal not due to a systematic RSD artefact. We conclude with a discussion of the caveats of our results and identify potential sources of PV.

By projecting the 4PCF onto spherical harmonics, they evaluate whether parity-odd RSD components survive spatial volume averaging in the standard isotropic 4PCF estimator. This allows to extend the fermionic dark mass range possibly down to $m_\chi \sim 10^7$~GeV, depending on $T_{\rm RH}$ and the dark QED coupling. We also determine under which conditions the hidden sector reaches thermal equilibrium and derive a lower bound on the temperature ratio at reheating $(T'/T)_{\rm RH}$ as function of the dark QED coupling and the reheating temperature.

They demonstrate that while standard bremsstrahlung does not lift this suppression due to the conformal invariance of the dark QED stress-energy tensor, the trace anomaly of dark QED provides an alternative production channel via a Dalitz-like process. This mechanism allows for significantly lighter dark fermions, potentially down to $m_\chi \sim 10^7$ GeV, depending on the reheating temperature and the dark gauge coupling.
conclusions: The minimal gravitational production of dark fermions is helicity-suppressed, requiring $m_\chi \gtrsim 10^{10}$ GeV to match the observed relic abundance.
The trace anomaly of dark QED enables a new production channel for dark fermions, effectively bypassing the helicity suppression.
For a dark gauge coupling $e' \simeq 1$, the viable dark matter mass range is extended downwards to $m_\chi \sim 10^7$ GeV for a reheating temperature $T_{\rm RH} \sim 10^{14}$ GeV.
Sequential production of dark fermions via dark photon annihilation is found to be sub-leading compared to the anomaly-induced Dalitz process.

papers.title: Little Red Dots from Small-Scale Primordial Black Hole Clustering
papers.authors: Borui Zhang, Wei-Xiang Feng, Haipeng An
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations have identified a class of compact galaxies at high redshifts ($4 \lesssim z \lesssim 8$), dubbed "little red dots" (LRDs). The supermassive black holes (SMBHs) of $10^{5-8}{\rm\,M}_{\odot}$ in LRDs favor a heavy-seed origin. We propose a mechanism for their formation: Clusters of primordial black holes, formed through long-short mode coupling on small scales in the early Universe, undergo sequential mergers over extended timescales. This mechanism can evade cosmic microwave background distortions and result in heavy-seed SMBHs via runaway mergers. We employ Monte Carlo simulations to solve the Smoluchowski coagulation equation and determine the runaway merging timescale. The resulting stochastic gravitational wave background offers a distinctive signature of this process, and our model suggests highly spinning SMBHs at their formation if they inherit the spin residual of the cluster from tidal fields.

papers.title: Cosmological inference with halo clustering reconstructed from the redshift-space galaxy distribution
papers.authors: Ryuichiro Hada, Teppei Okumura
papers.abstract: Accurate modeling of small-scale redshift-space clustering is crucial for full-shape redshift-space distortion (RSD) analyses, where satellite galaxies contribute to one-halo terms and Finger-of-God distortions. We investigate halo reconstruction based on the cylinder grouping method of Okumura et al., Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 469, 459 (2017), which selects an effective halo center tracer from the observed galaxy distribution, and how it impacts cosmological parameter inference. Using luminous red galaxy mock catalogs from the AbacusSummit simulations at $z=1.1$, we perform effective field theory (EFT)-based full-shape modeling of the power spectrum of the reconstructed-halo sample. We show that the dominant reconstruction-induced systematics can be described and incorporated within the standard EFT framework. In particular, a simple multipole-dependent rescaling inferred directly from the data on large scales captures the dominant effect, while residual small-scale changes are absorbed by the standard counterterm and stochastic sector, without introducing additional reconstruction-specific parameters. The reconstructed-halo sample yields unbiased constraints on cosmological parameters, including the growth rate $f\sigma_{s8}$ and Alcock-Paczynski parameters. Compared to the galaxy sample, it enables both improved robustness and increased statistical precision: at the fiducial limit of $k_{\max}=0.2\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$, the uncertainty on $f\sigma_{s8}$ is reduced by more than $20\%$, while the high-$k_{\max}$ diagnostics show comparatively stable goodness of fit and nuisance parameters.

papers.title: Bispectrum BAO and the baryon-dark matter relative velocity
papers.authors: Adriana Nadal-Matosas, Héctor Gil-Marín, Licia Verde
papers.abstract: We evaluate the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) signal in the bispectrum as a tool to detect and characterize the relative velocity effect. We extend the existing framework by presenting an updated model for the redshift-space tree-level bispectrum that comprehensively incorporates all relative velocity terms. We introduce a novel, unbiased technique to extract the isotropic BAO dilation parameter ($\alpha_{\rm iso}$) solely from the bispectrum monopole. Validated against N-body simulations, this template-based extraction successfully recovers the acoustic scale and enhances the statistical constraining power by $\sim30\%$, when analyzed in tandem with the pre-reconstruction power spectrum, offering a powerful complement to standard post-reconstruction pipelines. We quantify how individual relative velocity components distort both two- and three-point statistics. We find that these effects induce distinct systematic shifts in the extracted $\alpha_{\rm iso}$ between the two probes. We find systematic discrepancies of up to $2\%$ for $b_{v^2}=\pm0.05$ and up to $20\%$ for $b_{\delta^{bc}}\le-2$. This differences demonstrate that a direct comparison of independent power spectrum and bispectrum BAO measurements can break parameter degeneracies and isolate the amplitude of these biases. Finally, we provide a concrete prescription to detect and constrain the three associated relative velocity bias parameters, showing that a joint analysis is highly sensitive to the $b_{v^2}$ and $b_{\delta^{bc}}$ amplitudes. This establishes the bispectrum BAO as a robust cosmological probe for current and next-generation galaxy surveys, serving both as a cross-check for standard analyses and a crucial diagnostic tool against systematic biases.

papers.title: The road towards precision measurements of $H_0$ with bright sirens in the Einstein Telescope era
papers.authors: Chiara De Leo, Elsa M. Teixeira, Vivian Poulin
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave standard sirens provide an independent probe of cosmic expansion since their luminosity distances are inferred directly from the gravitational-wave signal and, for bright sirens (BSs), the source redshifts are obtained through the identification of electromagnetic counterparts. In this work, we forecast the constraining power of future bright siren catalogues on the Hubble constant using simulated binary-neutron-star mergers detected by the Einstein Telescope with associated electromagnetic counterparts. We construct mock catalogues with different numbers of events and redshift distributions, with GW170817 as a reference BS, and analyse the resulting constraints within a flat $\Lambda$CDM cosmology. We find that, when bright sirens are used as a standalone probe, most of the information on $H_0$ is provided by low-redshift events, with the improvement in precision saturating for sources above $z \sim 1$; beyond that redshift, the constraining power of BSs is increasingly limited by the degeneracy with $\Omega_m$, which prevents further gains in precision on $H_0$. In this case, approximately $90$ low-redshift BSs are required to reach $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 1\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, while about $45$ are sufficient for $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 2\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$. When external BAO information is included to reduce the $H_0 - \Omega_m$ degeneracy, intermediate-redshift sirens become more informative and the required number of events decreases substantially, to roughly $20$ and $15$ BSs for $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 1\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\sigma_{H_0} \sim 2\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, respectively. These results highlight the importance of both electromagnetic counterpart identification and complementary background probes in making BSs a competitive, distance-ladder-independent test of the Hubble tension.

papers.title: Domain walls through different cosmologies
papers.authors: I. Dankovsky, D. Gorbunov, S. Ramazanov, A. Vikman
papers.abstract: We study properties of domain walls (DWs) arising in the model with a double well potential assuming different early universe cosmologies: from dust through stiff matter domination to the limit of effective Minkowski space. Using lattice simulations we demonstrate that evolution of DW networks exhibits an approximate universality with respect to the cosmological equation of state (EoS). Namely, the wall area inside a given large volume is mainly determined by the particle horizon, while details of cosmic expansion play a subdominant role. As it follows, particle horizon rather than the inverse Hubble rate is pivotal in DW evolution defining the network correlation length and hence its phenomenology, e.g., the characteristic wavelength of emitted gravitational waves (GWs). Formation of closed DWs is shown to be very sensitive to the cosmological EoS and hence violate the universality, but their contribution to the total network is too small to change the overall picture. The universality breaking is also observed in the spectral properties of GWs from annihilating (biased) DWs: i) the IR slope of the spectrum depends on the EoS parameter; ii) there is a plateau in the UV part of the spectrum, which gets more pronounced as one stiffens the EoS. However, the dependence on the EoS is rather weak in the near peak region, which is most relevant from the viewpoint of pulsar timing arrays and other searches for the stochastic GW background. For a selection of primordial cosmologies, we provide fitting formulae for the spectra near the peak.

papers.title: Dark Matter Constraints from Small-Scale Cosmic Structure
papers.authors: Ethan O. Nadler, Keir K. Rogers, Alex Drlica-Wagner
papers.abstract: Small-scale cosmic structure provides a powerful test of the fundamental nature of dark matter. A wide range of dark matter models impact matter clustering on small scales, including warm, fuzzy, and (self-)interacting dark matter. In these scenarios, dark matter physics such as free-streaming, wave interference, and self/Standard Model interactions alter the abundance and internal structure of dark matter halos. Cosmological and astrophysical probes of small-scale structure---including dwarf galaxies, strong lensing, the Lyman-$\alpha$ forest, stellar streams, and high-redshift galaxies---are therefore sensitive to these effects. Here, we review dark matter constraints provided by small-scale structure, focusing on observables that probe scales smaller than $\sim 1~\mathrm{Mpc}$, which define the frontier of current measurements. We summarize how these constraints have been translated to limits on microphysical dark matter models, and we discuss key modeling uncertainties and observational systematics. Finally, we highlight the growing importance of probe combination and simulation-based inference for this field, and we overview upcoming observational facilities that will sharpen small-scale structure tests of dark matter physics.

papers.title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
papers.authors: Paul Rogozenski, Sukhdeep Singh, Jonathan Blazek, Rachel Mandelbaum, Hung-Jin Huang, Ananth Tenneti
papers.abstract: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are an important source of systematic uncertainty in weak gravitational lensing measurements and also serve as a test for models of galaxy formation and evolution. These galaxy alignments are usually modeled assuming that the IA are sourced by the tidal fields around the galaxies. However, galaxy properties, like their proximity to other galaxies and their mass, provide alignment contributions beyond the tidal field. In this work, we perform novel model-agnostic tests to determine the impact of density-weighting on the IA of galaxies using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and SDSS-III (BOSS). We show that the primary effect of density-weighting is an increase of the alignment amplitude at large scales, whereas the small-scale impact is sample-dependent. We also assess the tidal alignment paradigm for IllustrisTNG galaxies using two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes, tidal fields, and the sampled background tidal field of the simulation box. We find, given the precision of our measurements, that central galaxies align linearly to the underlying (non-linear) tidal field well into the 1-halo regime.

papers.title: Minimal vacuum histories beyond $Λ$CDM: model comparison within VCDM
papers.authors: Antonio De Felice, Eleonora Di Valentino, Luis A. Escamilla, Jack Zidich
papers.abstract: Recent cosmological observations motivate alternatives to $\Lambda$CDM with evolving dark energy. We compare three such models, each introducing one additional cosmological parameter: F42, with equation of state $w(a)=w_0/\sqrt{a}$, and two smooth sign-changing effective dark-energy profiles, Ag and Qui. All models are implemented within VCDM, which determines the background and linear perturbations without introducing an additional propagating gravitational degree of freedom. We use CMB observations from SPT, Planck, and ACT, combined with DESI DR2 distance measurements, with and without the DESY5 Dovekie supernova sample. All three alternatives improve the best-fit likelihood relative to $\Lambda$CDM. When supernovae are included, the Akaike information criterion favors F42, while Ag and Qui remain nearly indistinguishable from $\Lambda$CDM on this criterion. The Bayesian evidence, however, does not establish a robust preference among the three alternatives. Our results show that improved fits to current observations can arise from physically different dark-energy histories, motivating complementary measurements of expansion and structure growth to distinguish them.

papers.title: The Sound of Dark Sectors in Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.authors: Amitayus Banik, Yanou Cui, Yu-Dai Tsai, Yuhsin Tsai
papers.abstract: A phase transition in the dark sector (DS) presents a promising explanation for the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) signals detected in recent observations by Pulsar Timing Arrays (PTAs). Instead of focusing solely on fitting data with phenomenological parameters, we systematically delineate simple, underlying DS models at the microscopic, Lagrangian level and uncover the conditions required to yield the GW spectrum observed by PTAs. Within this framework, the characteristic scale of the dark sector is $O$(MeV), with complementary tests at future energy- and intensity-frontier experiments.

papers.title: The Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA)
papers.authors: Dylan Nelson, Celine Peroux, Philipp Richter, Matthew M. Pieri, Sebastian Lopez, Rongmon Bordoloi, Siwei Zou, Joseph N. Burchett, Rebecca L. Davies, Rahul Ramesh, Matthew C. Smith, Sanchayeeta Borthakur, Christopher W. Churchill
papers.abstract: We create the first large-scale mock spectroscopic survey of gas absorption sightlines traversing the interstellar medium (ISM), circumgalactic medium (CGM), and intergalactic medium (IGM) surrounding galaxies of virtual Universes. That is, we create mock, or synthetic, absorption spectra by drawing lines-of-sight through cosmological hydrodynamical simulations, using a new mesh-free Voronoi ray-tracing algorithm. The result is the Synthetic Absorption Line Spectral Almanac (SALSA), which is publicly released on our online science platform. It spans a diverse range of ions, transitions, instruments, observational characteristics, modeling assumptions, redshifts, and numerical simulations. These include, but are not limited to: (ions) HI, OI, CI, MgI, MgII, FeII, SiII, CaII, ZnII, SiIII, SiIV, NV, CII, CIV, OVI; (instruments) SDSS-BOSS, KECK-HIRES, UVES, COS, DESI, 4MOST, WEAVE, XSHOOTER; (model choices) with/without dust depletion, noise, quasar continua, foregrounds; (redshift) from z=0 to z~6; (ancillary data) integrated equivalent widths, column densities, distances and properties of nearby galaxies; (simulations) IllustrisTNG including TNG50, TNG-Cluster, EAGLE, and SIMBA. We also provide Faraday rotation measure (RM) probing magnetic fields, and dispersion measure (DM) as traced by fast radio bursts (FRBs). The resulting dataset is generic and broadly applicable, enabling diverse science goals such as: (i) studies of the underlying physical gas structures giving rise to particular absorption signatures, (ii) galaxy-absorber and halo-absorber correlations, (iii) virtual surveys and survey strategy optimization, (iv) stacking experiments and the identification of weak absorption features, (v) assessment of data reduction methods and completeness calculations, (vi) inference of physical properties from observables, and (vii) apples-to-apples comparisons between simulations and data.

papers.title: Affine ANEC selects the closed FRW branch for geodesically complete cosmology
papers.authors: Nathan L. Burwig, Damien A. Easson
papers.abstract: Using the affinely parameterized averaged null energy condition (ANEC) along radial null geodesics, we prove that, within the globally nondegenerate Friedmann--Robertson--Walker (FRW) class with $a(t)>0$ for all cosmic times, non-static flat models and all open models cannot be both null geodesically complete and ANEC-satisfying. Bounded oscillatory or cyclic flat/open models obey the same obstruction; in non-static periodic cases the negative affine-ANEC contribution accumulates over infinitely many cycles, giving $I_{\rm ANEC}=-\infty$. The sign obstruction is absent in closed $(k=+1)$ FRW geometry, where positive curvature can offset the negative expansion contribution to the affine ANEC, allowing nonsingular, geodesically complete cosmologies with ordinary NEC-respecting matter. We construct closed-FRW scalar-field models and contrast them with their flat realizations, which require NEC-violating support. We show that neglecting small positive curvature in a flat reconstruction of the expansion history can produce an apparent phantom equation of state, with a percent-level shift at $z=1$. Our main result is a curvature classification of ANEC-compatible eternal FRW cosmologies within this class: non-static flat and all open models are obstructed, while the closed branch admits explicit complete realizations, with global de Sitter as the vacuum representative.

papers.title: Binary neutron stars in the next-generation era: multimessenger detection prospects and constraints on the equation of state, mass distribution, and cosmology
papers.authors: Hauke Koehn, Thibeau Wouters, Gilad Sadeh, Peter T.H. Pang, Mattia Bulla, Chris Van Den Broeck, Michael W. Coughlin, Tim Dietrich
papers.abstract: Next-generation gravitational-wave (GW) observatories will provide crucial insights into the nature of neutron star (NS) matter and the cosmological expansion history. We estimate the number of multimessenger detections of binary neutron stars (BNS) with the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) and project the resulting constraints on the equation of state (EOS), BNS mass distribution, and cosmology using joint hierarchical Bayesian inference. Our results rely on specific assumptions for the merger rate, EOS, and mass distribution; we consider two different mass functions, a narrow one centred around 1.4 $M_\odot$ and a wide one ranging from 1.1 to 2 $M_\odot$, and a merger rate with a local value of 107 Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$. Under this setup, our mock follow-up algorithm results in between $\sim40$ and $\sim100$ short-term electromagnetic counterparts per year for ET, depending on the detector layout and mass distribution. In a joint network with CE, this number ranges from $\sim 100$ to $\sim500$. Additionally, we project tens to hundreds of late-time afterglow detections from gamma-ray bursts or kilonovae (KNe). Based on the generated multimessenger events, we perform an injection campaign to hierarchically recover the EOS, mass distribution, and cosmology in a fully Bayesian framework. Focusing on KN events from ET alone, the multimessenger data from our largest analysed catalogue with 78 events can constrain the canonical NS radius $R_{1.4}$ to $\lesssim 0.2$ km and the Hubble constant $H_0$ to $\lesssim 1$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, at least in absence of systematic modelling offsets. By comparing inference results that are solely based on GW data and those incorporating light-curve information, we find that while the latter has negligible impact on the EOS constraints, it can benefit the inference of cosmological parameters.

papers.title: Quasicrystalline Inflation: From the Cosmological Dipole to Primordial Diffraction
papers.authors: Jiro Soda
papers.abstract: We propose quasicrystalline inflation. Six quasiperiodic phases decompose into three phonons and three phasons. It turns out that a coherent pure-phason displacement can generate a local power dipole while the linear traceless quadrupole vanishes. From spatially varying quadratic effective field theory, we derive off-diagonal correlations whose momentum transfer is restricted to integer combinations of the six icosahedral wavevectors. These correlated off-diagonal signals provide a characteristic observational signature of primordial quasiperiodic order, primordial diffraction.
